title: JGP Call: Forecast Points to Cuts Soon, but Not a Series; 'Sufficient' Was Not Guidance
summary: In a private call with JGP (with Franz Ruch also on the line), Fowkes describes policy as moderately restrictive after 50bp of hikes, with real rates high by historical standards, and is fairly confident inflation will start falling in a few months as base effects unwind; the November forecast looks easy, with Brent and the rand close to September assumptions after the US midterms, and the fuel-levy cut is a near-term development to look through. He reads the services pressure as largely pre-existing and tied to expectations not yet adjusted to the new 3% target rather than as second-round effects of the oil shock, and says the SARB may have put too much weight on the BER two-year-ahead expectations measure. Most notably, he says the forecast suggests the SARB will be able to start cutting 'relatively enthusiastically fairly soon', though he would be surprised by a whole series of cuts from January given El Niño, exchange-rate and advanced-economy tightening risks; El Niño is a risk, not baseline, for the committee majority. He also walks back the Governor's Oct. 29 'prevailing settings are sufficient' line as a description of the QPM rather than forward guidance, keeping further tightening on the table if inflation stays above target for substantially longer than 12-18 months. This is his first record in the base; relative to Kganyago's Oct. 29 dinner speech (hold with a tightening bias), the call leans to an easing path within the forecast while preserving the hawkish conditional and the '3% means 3%' credibility goal.

key_quotes.quote: The way I'm looking at this is that our forecast suggests we'll be able to start cutting rates relatively enthusiastically fairly soon.
key_quotes.context: Forecast-implied easing path, framed by the El Niño and FX risks.

key_quotes.quote: But I'd be surprised if we ended up with a whole series of cuts lined up starting in January.
Making a promise that we've done enough on rates and won't need to do anything more was definitely not the intention.
key_quotes.context: Walks back the Governor's 'settings are sufficient' line as QPM description, not guidance.

key_quotes.quote: I think they reflect the fact that people aren't yet used to the new inflation target. Expectations haven't shifted sufficiently lower.
key_quotes.context: Services pressure read as pre-existing/target-transition, not oil second-round effects.
